title: Entanglement-enabled Criticality in One-dimensional Quantum Contact Process
authors: Ya-Xin Xiang, Tianyi Yan, Weibin Li, Yu-Qiang Ma
abstract: The contact process is a paradigmatic example of nonequilibrium dynamics, with broad applications ranging from chemistry to sociology. Its quantum counterpart, the quantum contact process (QCP), extends the classical model to include coherent processes. Despite sustained interest, the nature of the transition in the one-dimensional (1D) QCP remains debatable. Here, combining Liouvillian spectral analysis, the tensor jump method, exact quantum jump Monte Carlo, and truncated Wigner simulations, we show that 1D QCP undergoes a continuous absorbing-state phase transition, with critical exponents distinct from the classical case. We further find Liouvillian gap closes well below the critical point, highlighting that spectral gap analysis alone cannot distinguish a phase transition from metastability in the QCP. Crucially, the 1D QCP is weakly entangled, yet even this weak entanglement is indispensable for capturing the correct critical behavior, whereas semiclassical methods artificially stabilize the active state and predict a spurious first-order transition. Our work establishes the quantum origin of the phase transition in the 1D QCP and underscores the essential role of entanglement in dissipative quantum many-body systems.
summary: This work analyzes the quantum phase transition in the 1D Quantum Contact Process, finding it to be a continuous transition. The authors prove that weak quantum entanglement is crucial for obtaining the correct critical exponents, showing that semiclassical methods fail by predicting an incorrect first-order transition. It underscores the fundamental role of entanglement in understanding quantum non-equilibrium dynamics.
main_problem: The paper investigates the nature of the absorbing-state phase transition (APT) in the 1D Quantum Contact Process (QCP) and determines the essential role of quantum entanglement in this transition.
main_result: The 1D QCP undergoes a continuous APT with critical exponents distinct from the classical case, demonstrating that weak entanglement is indispensable for capturing the correct critical behavior.
method: The study employs a combination of Liouvillian spectral analysis, Tensor Jump Method (TJM), and comparison with semiclassical approximations like the Truncated Wigner Approximation (OSDTWA).
model_or_system: The system is the Quantum Contact Process (QCP) on a 1D lattice, whose dynamics are governed by a Lindblad master equation involving coherent activation and dissipative processes.
key_observables: Active density ($n$), Liouvillian spectral gap, and entanglement entropy ($S(t)$).
important_parameters: Facilitation rate ($\Omega$) and the bond dimension ($\chi$) used in the TJM.
main_assumptions: The analysis compares results obtained using entanglement-preserving methods (TJM/QJMC) against those that neglect entanglement (OSDTWA).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the transition boundary ($\Omega_c$), the spectral gap behavior, and compare the time decay of the active density $n(t)$ across different methods, highlighting the failure of semiclassical approaches.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the QCP model, analyzes the transition using multiple advanced techniques, contrasts the results with semiclassical limits, and concludes by quantifying the necessity of entanglement for correct critical exponents.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous demonstration of how quantum coherence and entanglement are necessary ingredients to correctly describe non-equilibrium phase transitions in open quantum systems, distinguishing quantum criticality from classical or mean-field predictions.
